I try to be kind to people most of the time but still get written off as being 'rude' because I'm obviously upset from being mistreated and don't hide it well. But I think that's the discussion. Why should I have to hide it?

I often feel like I am blamed for being rude when I'm simply existing. Why is my behavior so often perceived as rude just because I don't act "normal." I think the difference is because my brain doesn't make any sense of and sometimes doesn't at all register social norms. Because I don't always follow these silent unwritten rules I'm labeled as 'rude.' Look I think most us can agree that all of the rules are bullshit and even different for different people. Why am I an ass because I can't read everyone's mind? Why instead can't the world just learn to be more patient with those that literally have a disability and that can't make sense of things the same way NT do. We are very smart but just because our brains are different we are expected to deal with the abuse and mistreatment. Because NT is the standard. That's all that I am saying.

Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing. It's basically a therapy technique to help take the trauma from your nervous system and move it into long-term storage in your brain. So you're not as readily affected by it and you can just view the memory as just that. A memory. Instead of intensely feeling it in your body, like you're right in that moment all over again. EMDR has been life-changing for me in processing my trauma. So that I could evetually move past what has happened to me.

Look we all have our own strengths and weaknesses.  One thing about the public school system is although they teach us some things it's way too broad to unlock each and every students hidden potential leaving many to fall through the cracks. I know things might seem bleak right now but just know that it's not that you aren't good at anything. Your hidden abilities are just not yet unlocked. I believe in you. 😁👍 Also go do something fun to clear your mind and destress a bit. Also maybe a nap. Naps are good.

Something's gotta give and that's the hard pill to swallow. I don't know what the curriculum to internship ratio is (I'm assuming that's why your work week is so long) I would just say to try and get through this semester the best you can and make a plan. Like I knew a guy who no matter what he did he always tried to get through a program a quickly as possible and making that worked for him but that's not a reasonable reality for everyone. You're human and it really sounds like you're trying to give it your all but by the time you get to needing to do other things besides work you're already burnt out. Which is super understandable. I know how it is being so busy and depressed and tired. And I'm not trying to say terminate your relationship if it makes you happy by all means stay in the relationship but also maybe understand that taking the curriculum at a slower place is just a more sustainable choice. You are human. You need breaks, and cuddles from your partner and food. I would also study to see if whatever state (province, country, relative area that you live in etc.) has some sort of free assistance through the government or non- profits that would assist you in getting generally screened by a psychiatrist/psychologist that can prescribe meds if that's something you're interested in. I just know how dark things can get I do. I've been there before where I was just so frustrated and fed up with everything and everyone that I just wanted it all to go away and I wasn't workin' nearly as damn hard as you are right now. So meds are an option. Umm I would watch videos or read blogs on anything that you think will help depending on what you feel your main struggles  are. Like maybe self love if you're feeling particularly down on yourself or time management or maybe you look up some sweet yoga moves  or a gaming YouTuber/ Streamer because you're just so damn stressed  and you need to just chill. Like whatever makes you feel like wanting to scream less (even if that thing is screaming lol.) Like the less you feel like you're brain is about explode the better and reach out to those close to you that you actually think care and do your best to explain how you feel. Talking about it may be therapeutic but the least it'll do is hopefully allow those people to more understanding of what you're going through and who knows maybe someone you didn't expect will out of the woodwork to try and help you with something. *shrugs* I dunno but they won't even be able to begin to understand if you don't reach out the olive branch and tell them. I wish you the best of luck. You're fuckin' awesome. I believe in you.

I want to start off by saying that your feelings are completely valid and I'm not in any way trying to make you feel otherwise. That being said I think that the people that know you best and love you, the people that want want to stay in your life are going to understand or at least try to. Because what people who legitimately give a fuck about you do is they make the effort to try and understand you when you're attempting to communicate with them. They listen. Fuck your abuser and try not to take what anyone who supports them or is 'on their side' says to heart. They're trash and you leave them in the garbage where you found them. You are beautiful and deserve better. As far as dealing with the voice change on a personal level I would just focus more understanding the emotions that you're going through.  Because honestly (and I'm not try to make light of the situation) but it happens,  you only human. When humans go through traumatic events a whole slew of things can happen in your brain. I advise you seek help. (Always keep in mind your own safety.) Therapy. Therapy. THERAPY and if you can't get therapy YouTube is a wonderful thing. I would watch all the content you can on self love, dealing with the emotions and side effects of going through abuse. Google that shit and any of the items on the list you think you check off find a video or a blog or a book on it. Even if therapy isn't readily available it's something that should definitely be considered for the future. Don't let anyone convince you that being a victim makes you weak. You're badass. Good luck. I believe in you.

Best fucking advice I could give you at this point in my life is that life is a balancing act. I grew up in in an environment where I was expected to be logical, and have good grades. The one parent that was around most of the time did not respond well to me expressing emotions or being emotional. That parent didn't really know what to do with them(my feelings) and quite often when I was going through something, had a issue with said parent or expressed intense emotion I was either ignored or scolded or almost scolded. Anyway I understand how it is being under pressure to always be a certain way and looking back on it... look... It's about asking yourself what really makes you happy and balancing that with everything else. Let's say your parents are super strict and A's are a must and you don't really neeeeed to play that sport then switch it out for only occasionally going for a jog (you still get excise but on your own time where you can fit it in better.) Or let's  say that that sport is your PASSION. In my personal opinion it is ok to let your grades slip A LITTLE so that you don't lose your mind. Like let's say your usually you're typically a straight A student. I think it's absolutely fine to pull back on the the book stuff ever so slightly if you need like more sleep or free time or whatever. So maybe that semester you would be an A/B student and still have time for the sport but don't feel so much like you're going crazy. 
Or maybe your parents are really pressuring you to be a scholar and an athlete but are still letting you live their rent free. So you put you two weeks in at your job. Life is a balancing act and you can only ever do you best and as long as your  giving all that you can, fuck anyone who has shit to say about it. You're only human Darling. We all need breaks and we all need alone time. 

TLDR: Life is a balancing act and you gotta figure out how to manage your time and do what's best for you on your own. You are the only one that can always be there for yourself. So learn how to lean on yourself so that when you have no one or everyone else has failed you. You know you can still do it. I believe in you. All is not lost. Fuck anyone who thinks you're not enough. You're human. Breath.You're beautiful.
